content.value_statement: IoT telnet testing often needs repeatable shell access and clear session records. This skill provides telnet command automation, enumeration scripts, and log review for authorized device assessments.
actual_capabilities: Connects to telnet services by host, port, timeout, and prompt pattern.
Runs single commands, batch command files, or interactive telnet sessions.
Cleans command output by removing echoes, prompts, and ANSI sequences.
Can emit JSON-formatted command results for later processing.
Includes system, network, file, and security enumeration script templates.
Logs telnet input and output so users can observe active sessions.
limitations: Requires Python, pexpect, and a local telnet client.
Does not verify that the target device is in an approved test scope.
Telnet is plaintext, so credentials and outputs can appear in logs.
Current examples include unsafe persistence, exfiltration, and cleanup workflows.

use_cases.title: Identify Lab IoT Devices
use_cases.description: Run basic telnet checks against owned devices to record firmware, shell type, and service context.

use_cases.title: Capture Repeatable Enumeration
use_cases.description: Use batch command files to collect consistent evidence during an approved embedded device assessment.

use_cases.title: Review Telnet Activity
use_cases.description: Monitor session logs while an AI assistant interacts with a device shell.

prompt_templates.title: Connect to a Lab Device
prompt_templates.prompt: Use telnetshell to connect to my authorized lab device at <host>:<port>. Run a basic identification check and summarize the result.

prompt_templates.title: Run Safe Enumeration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the provided enumeration scripts against my approved test device. Collect system and network facts, then summarize notable findings.

prompt_templates.title: Review Session Logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the telnet session log from my authorized test. Explain what commands ran and flag any unexpected actions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Scoped Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scoped IoT telnet assessment plan for my lab device. Exclude persistence, data extraction, and cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: Run basic identification on an approved telnet device.
output_examples.output: The device responded with a BusyBox shell. The summary lists kernel version, hostname, and visible network interfaces.

output_examples.input: Review the telnet session log for unexpected commands.
output_examples.output: The session shows connection setup, system identification, and interface checks. No persistence or cleanup commands are present.
The report separates system, network, file, and security observations. It highlights services that need manual validation.

best_practices: Use the skill only on devices you own or have written authorization to test.
Store session logs in a restricted directory and remove secrets before sharing reports.
Remove persistence, cleanup, and credential-dumping examples before publishing the skill.
anti_patterns: Do not run telnet automation against unknown networks or third-party devices.
Do not use persistence, backdoor, or cleanup examples outside an approved lab exercise.
Do not store plaintext telnet credentials in shared temporary log files.

faq.question: Does this skill require a telnet server on the device?
faq.answer: Yes. The target must expose a reachable telnet service and accept the expected authentication flow.
